caption: Results of our model with different weights of negative samples.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the NPMI (Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information) scores achieved by three different models—20NG, IMDB, and NIPS—as a function of the weight assigned to negative sampling, ranging from 0.5 to 3.0. The x-axis, labeled “weight of negative sampling,” uses a linear scale and is marked at intervals of 0.5. The y-axis, labeled “NPMI,” also uses a linear scale, spanning from 0.18 to 0.42, with tick marks at intervals of 0.02. The plot displays three distinct lines: the 20NG model is represented by a black line with square markers, the IMDB model by a red line with circular markers, and the NIPS model by a blue line with triangular markers. The black line (20NG) starts at approximately 0.375 and trends slightly upward to about 0.382 before leveling off. The red line (IMDB) begins at approximately 0.200, dips slightly to around 0.195, rises to about 0.202, and then remains relatively flat near 0.200. The blue line (NIPS) begins at 0.400, peaks at approximately 0.415, then gradually declines to about 0.405.
